## Introduction

This note is a living reference: copy it to start a new note. Text, math, citations,
margin notes, and figures all work as below. Citations are numbered and show the
bibliography entry on hover [@zhang2017rethinking; @li2018visualizing].

Inline math looks like $\mathcal{L}(\theta) = \frac{1}{n}\sum_i \ell(f_\theta(x_i), y_i)$,
and display math can be numbered and referenced:

$$
\theta_{t+1} = \theta_t - \eta \, \nabla_\theta \mathcal{L}(\theta_t)
$$ {#eq-gd}

Gradient descent (@eq-gd) is the simplest optimizer.^[Footnotes go in the margin and also show on hover.]

::: {.column-margin}
**Margin note.** Any block wrapped in `.column-margin` sits in the right margin next to
the paragraph it follows.
:::

## Figures at three widths

Hover over a figure reference to preview the figure: @fig-curves shows a body-width
figure, @fig-grid a page-width one, and @fig-wide a full-screen one. Click a figure to zoom.

## Code

Code chunks that produce figures are hidden (`echo: false`). To *show* code, use a
plain code block; it gets a copy button:

```python
from plotting import plot_curves

plot_curves("results/curves.csv")
```
